M Liton Ahmed, Advocate with Sheikh Mosfeq Kabir, Advocates—For the Appellants. 
Abdus Salam Mondal, Advocate with Abul Kalam Azad, Advocates—For the Respondents.
parties:
Shadat Hossain Talukder and others…………Appellants
vs
Md Kalimuddin Patwary and others………..Respondents
full_judgment:
SM Emdadul Hoque J: This First appeal at the instance of the defendant appellants is directed against the judgment and decree dated 26-11-1974 passed by the subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Partition Suit No. 89 of 1967 decreeing the suit with costs against the defendant Nos. 1(Ka)-1(Kha) the defendant Nos. 2-5, 6-18 and 55-63 and expertly without costs against the rest.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the appeal, in short, is that the respondents as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 89 of 1967 before the subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla for partition of the suit land contending inter alia, that the property of schedule-1 belonged to Tofani in 12 arenas, Mohammed Ali in 4 annas and land of schedule-2 belonged to Tofani and Mohammed Ali in equal shares and the property of schedule-3 belonged to Tofani in 10 annas 13 gondas 1 kara and 1 kranti and Mohammed Ali 5 annas 6 gondas 2 karas 2 kranti i.e. /3rd and /3rd respectively. Mohammad Ali having owned and possessed the property in dispute in share died leaving behind the defendant No. 1 Abdul Hakim one son and three daughters defendant No. 1, Rokabjan, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Rupjan defendant No. 64 and defendant No. 65 Phuljan. Thus defendant No. 1 inherited 1 anna 12 ganda in schedule 1, 3 anna 4 gonda in schedule-2 and 2 anna 2 gonda 2 kara 2 kranti in schedule-2 and each of the daughters of Mohammed Ali inherited 16 gandas in schedule-1, 1 anna 12 gandas in schedule-2 and 1 anna 1 ganda 1 kara 1 kranti in schedule-3.

3. Rokabjan died leaving husband Nasiruddin Patwary, 3 sons plaintiff Nos. 11-12 and Amiruddin. Amiruddin died leaving plaintiff Nos. 1-2 as sons plaintiff No. 3 wife plaintiff Nos. 4-7 and Sabura Khatoon as daughters. Nasaruddin died leaving sons plaintiff Nos. 11-12. Sabura Khatoon died leaving husband plaintiff No. 10 and plaintiff Nos. 8-9 daughters and brothers as mentioned above. Thus the entire interest of Rokabjan inherited by the plaintiffs.

4. Phuljan defendant No. 65 sold her entire interest in the disputed property to 3 sons of Rokabjan by kabala dated 17th Falgun 1345 BS. In the same manner Rupjan defendant No. 64 also sold her entire interest to them by kabala dated 16th Kartick 1345 BS. Thus by purchase and by inheritance the plaintiffs acquired interest of 2 annas 8 gandas in schedule-1, 4 annas 16 gandas in schedule-2 and 3 annas 4 gandas in schedule-3 and they are in ejmali possession of the disputed property along with other co-shares.

5. Tofani died leaving sons Syed Ali and Amjad Ali and daughters Alekjan and Karimjan. Karimjan and Alekjan relinquished their interest in favour of their brother Syed Ali and Amjad Ali by registered Nababi deed. Thus Syed Ali and Amjad Ali acquired equal interest in the property left by Tofani. Syed Ali died leaving defendant Nos. 2-5 as heirs and Amjad Ali died leaving 6 sons defendant Nos. 6-10 and one Kala Miah, daughter defendant No. 11 and wife defendant 12 Kala Mia died leaving heirs defendants Nos. 13-18.

6. Amiruddin predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 1-10 purchased 0.09 cents from khatian No. 9 by kabala from defendant No. 6 and also purchased 0.07 cents from defendant No. 6 by another kabala from khatian No. 9 by two more kabalas Amiruddin purchased 0.101/4 cents from defendant No. 2 from khatian No. 9. Nasiruddin purchased 0.083/4 cents from defendant No. 2 by kabala dated 7th Falgun 1359 BS from khatian No. 9. Thus Amiruddin and Nasiruddin by purchase got 0.35 cents in which plaintiffs have acquired interest in addition to the share already mentioned. Plaintiff Nos. 1-2 and 11-12 sold 0.54 cents of land to defendant No. 5 subject to an agreement for reconveyance. The property having not been partitioned by metes and bounds, great in convenience is left in the matter of enjoyment of property Title Suit No. 111 of 1947 was filed but the said suit was ultimately with drawn on 30-5-64 with permission to sue afresh, defendant No. 1 having not succeeded to amicable partition of the disputed property. Thus filed the instant suit for partition.

7. The suit was contested by the defendant No. 1 by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. During the trial of the suit the defendant No. 1 died and the defendant No. 1 (Ka)-1 (Kha) being substituted and adopted the written statements filed by defendant No. 1. Their case is that the suit is not maintainable in the present from and that Tofani had 16 annas interest in schedule-1, 4 annas interest in schedule-2 and 10 annas 13 gandas-1 kara-1 kranti in schedule-3 and Mohammed Ali had 4 annas interest in schedule-2 and 5 annas 6 gondas 2 kara 2 kranti interest in schedule-3, the daughters of Mohammed Ali made oral gift of their interest in favour of defendant No. 1 in the year 1313 BS Defendant No. 1 and Phuljan were then minors when their father died and they were brought up in the house of Tofani Talukder who was related to Mohammed Ali Talukdar and Tofani Talukder being satisfied with the service of defendant No. 1 orally gifted 4 annas interest of schedule-1 property to him. The 8 annas interest of schedule-2 was in Khas possession out of the property, defendant No. 1 took lease of 4 annas and Syed Ali and Amjad Ali, sons of Tofani Talukder took bandabasta of 4 annas interest orally. In this way defendant No. 1 acquired 4 annas interest in schedule-1, 4 annas interest in schedule-2 and 3. Mohammad Ali Talukder obtained the portion of the land by way of gift from his sisters, as such, the entire interest of Mohammed Ali Talukder devolved on him. The allegations of the plaintiffs that they are in possession of the disputed property by inheritance and by purchase and they are in enjoyment of usufructs of the disputed property are false. The allegation's of transpires and inter transpires are false and collusive transactions and the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs.

8. The defendant Nos. 2-5 also contested the suit by filing separate written statement supporting the case of the plaintiffs and prayed for their Saham. The case of the defendant Nos. 2-5 is that Tofani had 12 annas interest in schedule-3, they are heirs of Syed Ali, son of Tofani. The daughters of Tofani relinquished their interest in favour of their brothers Syed Ali and Amjad Ali. They admitted that plaintiff No. 1 sold 54 cents of land to defendant No. 5 subject to reconveyance if consideration paid within the stipulated period. They claims 6 annas in schedule-1, 4 annas in schedule-2 and 5 annas 6 ganda 2 kara and 2 kranti in schedule-3 exclusively their transpires and further claims their purchased land from plaintiff No. 1.

9. The defendant Nos. 6-18 also contested the suit and claimed Saham. Their case is that they are the heirs and defendants of Amjad Ali son of Tofani and the heirs of Syed Ali and claimed Saham for 1.091/4 decimals by purchase from defendant cosharer of the suit land.

10. The defendant Nos. 55-63 also contested the suit by filing separate written statement and prayed for Saham for .91 decimals of land. They claimed that the defendant No. 1 sold 0.91 decimals to Moharjan Bibi wife of Haji Golam Ali Shiekh by registered kabala deed and she owing and possessing the same and gifted the said property by her husband in favour of these defendants by a heba deed dated 16-6-1947 and since then they are in possession of the suit land.

11. The trial court framed the following three issues:

1. Is the suit maintainable in the present from?

2. If the plaintiffs and the saham praying defendants are entitled to get their respective sahams as prayed for? 3. To what relief the plaintiffs and defendants who have prayed for saham are entitled?

12. At the trial the plaintiffs adduced 2 witnesses as PW-1 and PW-2 and the main contested defendant adduced one witness as DW-1 and other defendants examined rest 3 witnesses as DW-2—DW-4 in supported of their respective cases. The parties also produced some documentary evidence to prove their respective cases.

13. The trial court after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record decreed the suit and also gave saham to the parties as claimed by its judgment and decree dated 26-11-1974.

14. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant No. 1 (Ka)-1(Kha) preferred this appeal.

15. Mr Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Advocate with Mr Abul Kalam Azad, Advocate enter appeared on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents through vokalatnama to contest the Appeal.

16. Mr M Liton Ahmed, the learned Advocate with Mr Sheikh Mosfeq Kabir, Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellants submits that the trial court committed serious error in law in not considering the material facts of the case that the defendant Abdul Hakim Talukder the son of Mohammad Ali Talukder is the CS recorded owner and the three sisters of the defendants No. 1 did not take any step against the CS record even never claimed their saham but their successive heirs claimed saham without challenging the CS record. He further submits that not only the CS record even the SA and RS records were also prepared in the name of the defendant No. 1. He further submits that admittedly as per CS record the suit land belonged to Syed Ali and Amjad Ali sons of Tofani Talukder and Abdul Hakim Talukder son of Mohammad Ali Talukder and no dispute among them about the suit land but the trial court did not at all consider the said vital facts of the case. He further submits that the trial court committed patient illegality in decreeing the suit whereas it is settled principle that decree in case of partition cannot be given if the parties did not make prayer for declaration of title and challenging the record-of-rights which was prepared in the name of defendant No. 1 the predecessor of the present appellants. He further submits that the suit is not maintainable since CS operation was held on and between 1915-1919 and the instant suit was filed long after the CS record even thereafter the SA and RS record were also prepared but the plaintiffs did not challenge the said record-of-rights though they have knowledge about the records which the suit was clearly barred by limitation in support of his argument he referred the decision of the case of Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari and others reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81. The case of Md Sirajul Islam vs Taimuddin 13 ADC-349 and the case of Hriday Ranjan Dey vs Niranjan Dey being deed his hears Probate Dey reported in 10 BLT (AD) 137 = 54 DLR (AD) 16.

17. He further submits that as per provision of section 103 (b) (5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 every entry in a record-of-right finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect but the trial court did not consider the said provision of law and erroneously passed the impugned judgment.

18. His further contention is that the CS record of schedule No. 1 prepared in the name of two sons of Tofani, Syed Ali and Amjad Ali as 6 annas share each and Hakimuddin for 4 annas share and Schedule-2 the khatian No. 40 stands in the name of Syed Ali and Amjad Ali for 4 annas shares to each and Hakimuddin for 8 annas shares and Schedule-3 appertains to khatian No. 152, stands in the names of Syed Amjad Ali and Hakimuddin as 1/3 share each, but the trial court held that the name of Hakimuddin was wrongly entered though it has not been challenged by the plaintiffs as such the findings of the trial court cannot be sustained. He prayed for allowing the appeal.

19. On the contrary Mr Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Advocate along with Mr Abul Kalam Azad Advocate submits that the trial court rightly passed the impugned judgment. He further submits that the plaintiffs categorically stated that the suit land originally belonged to Tofani Talukder and Mohammed Ali Talukder but the CS record was wrongly prepared in the name of Syed Ali, and Amjad Ali son of Tofani Talukder and Abdul Hakim Talukder the son of Mohammad Ali Talukder and the plaintiffs are the successive heirs of Mohammad Ali Talukder and the trial court rightly found the same. He further submits that the presumption of correctness of the record-of-rights is to be rebuttable provided under section 103(b)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 and since the plaintiffs claimed that the CS record was wrongly prepared in the name of Abdul Hakim alone excluding the name of his three sisters namely, Rokabjan the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Phuljan defendant No. 64 and Rupjan defendant No. 65. He further submits that the trial court rightly found that the plaintiffs succeed to prove that the suit land was originally belonged to Mohammed Ali Talukder. The learned Advocate referred the case of Meherjan Bibi vs Naimuddin Dhali reported in 33 DLR (HCD) 126. He also referred the case of Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81.

20. He further submits that as per provision of section 103(b) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 and section 114 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, though the entry of the records-of-right has presumptive value and when the plaintiffs claimed their right then onus shifted upon the defendants. In support of his arguments he referred the decision of the case of Pramatha Nath Chowdhury vs Kamir Mondal reported in 11 DLR (SC) 392. His next argument is that though initially no prayer for declaration of title of the suit land but ultimately through amendment before this court the plaintiff-respondents amended the pleadings and claimed declaration of title of the suit land so, no question that the suit is not maintainable without any prayer for declaration of title. He prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

21. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment of the courts below, the papers and documents as available on the record.

22. To consider the case first we would like to discuss the evidence of PWs and DWs. 23. PW-1 Kalam Uddin Patwari the plaintiff No.1 deposed that he deposed himself and also on behalf of the other plaintiffs. He deposed that schedule-1 land belonged to Tofani in 12 annas and Mohammad Ali 4 annas. In schedule-2 Tofani had 8 annas and Mohammad Ali had 8 annas and in schedule-3 Tofani had 10 annas 13 gands 1 Kara 1 Kranti and Mohammad Ali had 5 annas 6 gands 2 Kars 2 Kranti. He further deposed that Mohammad Ali died leaving 3 daughters namely, Fuljan, Rupjan and Rukubjan and one son Abdul Halim defendant No.1 and Rukubjan died leaving her husband Nasiruddin and 3 sons Amiruddin, Aftabuddin and Usafuddin and Amiruddin died leaving 2 sons Karimuddin plaintiff No. 1, Ali Ahmed, plaintiff No. 2 and 5 daughters the plaintiff Nos. 4, 5, 6 and 7 and one Sabura (deceased) and wife Halima plaintiff No. 3. Sabaura died leaving husband Osman Trafdar the Plaintiff No. 10 and the daughters the plaintiff Nos. 8 to 9. Plaintiff Nos. 11 to 12 Aftabuddin and Wasimuddin sons of Rukubjan.

24. Tofani died leaving 2 sons Syed Ali and Amjad Ali and 2 daughters Karimjan and Alekjan. Amjad Ali died leaving 6 sons and one daughter and Syed Ali died leaving 3 sons and one daughter the defendant Nos; 2 to 5.

25. He deposed that Karimjan and Alekjan relinquished their interest in favour of Syed Ali and Amjad Ali the two brothers. Karimjan died leaving 2 sons 2 daughters and said two daughters of Karimjan died without any issue. Alekjan died leaving the defendant Nos. 67-71. He deposed that his father purchased land from Fuljan and Rupjan and the defendant Nos. 60-61 by kabala dated 17th Falgoon, 1345 BS and 16th Kartick, 1349 BS. He deposed that Plaintiff by inheritance obtained 2 anna and 8 gandas share in schedule-1 and 4 anna and 16 gands in schedule-2 and 3 anna and 4 ganda in schedule-3. He deposed that subsequently they purchased 0.35 cent and Amiruddin purchased from defendant No. 6 Ayub Ali by kabala dated 29-9-1949 AD and 4th Kartick 1356 BS corres-ponding to 21-10-1949. Nuruddin purchased land from Rahim Proksha by a kabala dated 71h Falgun, 1359 BS corres-ponding to 19-2-1953. Amairuddin purchased land from Rahim Baksha by two kabalas dated 12-3-1951 and 21-5-1952 AD.

26. He deposed that Plaintiffs sold 0.54 cents of land to defendant No. 5 by kabala deed dated 20-5-67 subject to reconveyance and they filed partition suit No. 111 of 1947 which was decreed finally but the defendants filed objection under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the said decree on the ground that the decree was passed against dead person and accordingly the said decree was set-aside. Hence, this suit. He stated that it is not a fact that Tofani was the sole owner of schedule-1 and that they did not make any oral gift in favour of defendant No. 1. He deposed that it is not a fact that Rukubjan and Phuljan made oral gift before 1323 BS. He deposed that the CS Khatian was not proper and has interest of all co-shares and they are in ejmali possession and prayed for saham.

27. In cross-examination this witness admitted that the plaintiff No. 12 is in court room and his chacha (uncle) Altabuddin is not in house and he is 35 years old. He stated that his father Amiruddin was a Mutwalli and was a pleader's clerk and Mohammad All was also a brother namely Aminuddin. Abdul Hakim is also known as Hakimuddin Talukder and he could not show any document that Mohammad Ali had 4 annas and Tofani had 12 annas share in schedule-I but they possessed accordingly. He stated that he has document to show that Mohammad All and Tofani had 8 annas share each in schedule-2 but yet filed that document and it is not a fact that Tofani had 16 annas in schedule-I and in schedule-II Mohammad Ali had 4 annas and Tofani had 4 annas and the remaining 8 annas khas land of the ex-landlord.

28. He has stated that it is not a fact that opposite party No.1 took bandabasta of 4 annas and Syed All and Amjad Ali 2 annas each and Tofani took bandabasta of 4. annas of scheduled-2 from the ex-landlords. It is not a fact that Mohammad All was the cousin (Mamato Bhai) of Tofani Talukdar. If is not a fact that Tofani gifted 4 annas interest to Abdul Hakim defendant No. 1 from schedule-I after the death of Mohammad Ali. The house of defendant No. 1 and their house are intervened by a Khal. It is not a fact that his father made tadbir at the time of CS operation. He stated that he had no knowledge that whose names the SA khatians have been prepared and did not take attempt to correct the SA khatian. He stated that it is not a fact that the sisters of defendant No. 1 gifted their property in his favour before CS operation and they are in possession of plot No. 271 and 272 and Plot Nos. 271 and 272 are bhitis and they purchased the same from Ayub All and Rahim Baksh and are in possession about 20 years. He stated that they have also possessed plot No. 285 and got it by purchased from Phuljan and Rupjan. He stated that it is not a fact that the kabalas are not correct and they have no possession in pursuance of kabalas and he stated that some of the documents were lost and damaged by rain water.

29. PW-2 Md Nawab Khan deposed that the parties are known to him. He deposed that he has land adjacent to the south of the disputed land and he is a Manager of the Co-operative Society, Chandpur and has collected loans and interest. He deposed that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land and it is not a fact that the sisters of defendant No. 1 gifted land to him. He deposed that the plaintiffs are in possession of the disputed property and he was about 8/9 years old at the time of CS operation and defendant No. 1 conducted the affairs for recording of their interest.

30. In cross-examination by the defendant this witness stated that he could not say the area of the disputed property and he had no speaking terms with the sisters of the defendant No. 1 but usually the sounds of the house of the defendant No. 1 came to our house. He stated that it is not his affairs to take any account who gifted the property in favour of whose and Hakimuddin was his contemporary. He stated that he could not remember that he saw Hakimuddin at the time of CS operation and could not say when Rukubjan and her sister took from the house of their brother. He stated that it is not a fact that he deposed falsely.

31. DW-1 Anwarullah Talukdar deposed that he is defendant No.I (Kha). Abdul Hakim Talukdar also known as Hakimuddin. He deposed that the Schedule-1 belonged to Mohammad Ali 4 annas khas, Tofani 4 annas and 8 annas and Khan Hakimuddin took settlement of 4 annas share. Syed All and Amajad Ali took bandabasta of 4 annas and schedule-3 belonged to the persons as alleged in the plaint. Mohammad Ali died in 1313 BS and at that time Hakimuddin was aged about 16/17 years. Tofani Talukdar looked after Hakimuddin during his minority. Rukubjan and Fuljan orally gifted their interest in favour of their brother Hakimuddin Talukdar and Tofani Talukdar accepted the gift on behalf of Hakimuddin Talukdar. Rupjan also orally gifted her interest in favour of Hakimuddin and Tofani gifted 4 annas interest of schedule-2 in favour of Hakimuddin before CS record. Hakimuddin had 4 annas in schedule-1 and 8 annas in schedule-2 and 1/3rd in schedule-3. He deposed that Amir Uddin Patwary got the interest recorded during the CS operation and he was a literate person of his relation. The kabalas in favour of the plaintiffs are fraudulent, collusive and bogus and were not acted upon. He deposed that the plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit for partition which was withdrawn by the plaintiffs and the grandsons of Tofani falsely filed this suit for harassing them. Karimjan and Alekjan relinquished their interest in favour of Syed Ali and Amjad Ali. It is not a fact that Mohammad Ali had 4 annas in schedule-1 and 8 arenas in schedule-2. It is not a fact that the CS Khatian was not correct. Rukubjan and her sisters never separated the homestead in dispute.

32. In cross-examination by the plaintiffs he stated that his present age is 35/36 years and he was not present when the oral gift was made by Rukubjan and others in favour of Hakimuddin and the persons who had knowledge of the oral gift all are dead. He stated that it is not a fact that there was no oral gift by Rukubjan and others in favour of Hakimuddin. He further denied that it is not true that Tofani did not gift his land in favour of Hakimuddin. He stated that he has no paper to state that the schedule-2 to the extent of 8 annas was settled in their favour and he has no paper to show that his father and sons of Tofani both made settlement of land of schedule-2 but stated that they have dakhila. He stated that he could not produce any witness to prove the factum of settlement and oral gift and it is not a fact that Mohammad Ali had 4 annas in schedule-1 and 8 annans in schedule-2 and Tofani had 8 annas share in schedule-2. He stated that after oral gift, the heirs of Rukubjan, Rupjan and Fuljan never leave or visit their house and they themselves also did not visit their house. Rukubjan died in the year 1941 AD. He stated that it is not a fact that Rukubjan and her sister visited their homestead and he did not see Amiruddin, supervising the works of record of interest and he was not present when the plaintiff got the kabala. He stated that it is not a fact that the plaintiffs are in possession of kabala land. He admitted that his father sold 0.91 cents to Meherjan wife of Golam Ali. Meherjan gifted the same to defendant Nos. 55-63 and they are in possession.

33. Md Nur Baksha Talukdar son of late Sayed Ali Talukder deposed as DW-2 on behalf of himself as defendant Nos. 4 and 5 on behalf of defendant Nos.1-4. He stated that Tofani had 12 annas in schedule-1 and 8 annas schedule-2 and 2/3rd in schedule-3 and Tofani died leaving sons Syed Ali and Amjad Ali and 2 daughters Karimajan and Alekjan who relinquished their interest in favour of Syed Ali and Amjad Ali. He deposed that defendant Nos. 2-5 are the heirs of Syed Ali who have 6 annas in schedule- 1, 4 annas in schedule-2, 5 annas, 6 Gands 2 Kara 2 Kranti in schedule-3. He denied that it is not a fact that Tofani gifted 4 annas of his interest in favour of Hakimuddin and Tofani had 4 annas interest in schedule-2 and 8 annas was in Khas of the Ex landlords. He deposed that it is not a fact that Hakimuddin took settlement of 4 annas by way of bandabasta. It is not a fact that his grandfather Tofani accepted gift on behalf of Rukubjan and her sister in favour of Hakimuddin. Defendant No. 5 purchased 0.54 cents of land from plaintiff No. 1 and defendant 5 is in possession of the same and deposed that the CS Khatian is correct.

34. In cross-examination he stated that plaintiffs are in possession of the disputed property and the sisters of Rupjan and her sons visited the homestead of defendant No. 1. He stated that the plaintiffs filed this suit and they are not involved in filing the suit. He stated that he did not see his grandfather Tofani. He stated that he had no knowledge who supervised the work of settlement operation and the schedule property belonged to Tofani and Mohammad Ali's predecessor. He stated that he had no knowledge about the gift made by Tofani. He stated that he did not see Mohammad Ali and could not show any document that Hakimuddin was minor when Mohammad Ali died and he made statements on the basis of purchase deed and Rukubjan died about 15/20 years back and they have no enmity with the defendant No. 1 and his son. It is not a fact that he deposed falsely.

35. DW-3, Fazlul Hoq the defendant No. 57 deposed in favour of defendant Nos. 55-63 in his deposition he stated that he is defendant No. 57 and deposed himself and on behalf of defendant Nos. 55- 63. He stated that defendant No. 1 sold, 0.91 cent to Meherjan who gifted the property to Shamsul Hoq and others defendant Nos. 55-63, and he filed heba deed and prayed for saham of 0.91 cent.

36. DW-4 Shamsul Haque the defendant No. 7 deposed in favour of defendant Nos. 6-18 in his deposition he stated that he support the case of the plaintiffs. He deposed that they are the heirs of Amajad Ali son of Tofani and claimed saham for 6 annas in schedule-1, 4 annas in schedule-2 and 5 annas 5 gands, 2 kara 2 kranti in schedule-3. He deposed that he purchased 1.091/4 acres by 9 kabalas and filed the said kabla and prayed for Saham.

37. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the side, perused the impugned judgment, the evidence of the witnesses and the papers and document as available on the record.

38. The case of the plaintiffs is that the suit land originally belonged to Mohammad Ali and Tofani Talukder. Admittedly, the CS record was prepared in the name of Syed Ali and Amjad Ali sons of Tofani Talukder and Abdul Hakim son of Mohammad Ali Talukder. It is admitted that Mohammad Ali Talukder leaving behind only son Abdul Hakim Talukder and three daughters Rukubjan the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Phuljan the defendant No. 64 and Rupjan the defendant No. 65. In the instant case some of the heirs of Mohammad Ali Talukder claimed partition of their ejmali land. The plaintiffs claimed that the suit land originally belonged to Mohammad Ali Talukder but inadvertently, the CS record was wrongly prepared only in the name of Abdul Hakim Talukder son of Mohammad Ali Talukder excluding the name of three daughters of Mohammad Ali. The plaintiff Nos. 1-7 are the successive heirs of Rukubjan. The plaintiff Nos. 6-12 also the successive heirs of deceased Amjad Ali. The defendant Nos. 11-12 also claimed that they have purchased the land from Phuljan the defendant No. 64 and Rupjan defendant No. 65.

39. In the instant case it is found that the DW-4 defendant No. 7 is the successive heirs of Tofani Talukder one of the son of Abdul Kader Talukder. The heirs of Amjad Ali Talukder, prayed for saham for 1.091/4 acres of land on the basis of 9 kabala deeds and the which were exhibited. There is no dispute about the land of two sons of Tofani Talukder by both the sides. Though DW-1 claimed that Tofani Talukder gifted some portion of land to them but he could not show any document in support of his claim. On perusal of the evidence of the DW 4 it cannot be presumed that he has supported the case of the plaintiffs though on stage he only deposed that he support the allegations of the plaintiffs nothing more.

40. On perusal of the evidence of DW-3 Fazlul Hoq, the defendant No. 57 who deposed in favour of himself and the defendant Nos. 55-63. In his deposition he categorically, stated that defendant No. 1 sold 91 decimals of land to one Meherjan who gifted the property to Shamsul Haque and others the defendant Nos. 55-63. In support he filed the heba deed and claimed saham for 91 decimals of land. The defendant No. 1 did not cross-examine the said witness. Furthermore the DW 1 also admitted the same. From the aforesaid facts that the claimed of this defendants is proved.

41. Defendant Nos. 6-18 are the successive heirs of Tofani Talukder and heirs of Amjad Ali one of the son of Tofani Talukder and they claimed their saham by inheritance and also claimed 1.091/4 acres of land on the basis of purchase deed. The trial court gave saham to them.

42. Admittedly, the CS record was prepared in the name of Syed Ali and Amjad Ali the son of Tofani Talukder and Abdul Hakim Talukder son of Mohammad Ali Talukder. Plaintiff case is that though the CS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Hakim Talukder the only son of Mohammad Ali Talukder excluding his sisters but the property belonged to Mohammad Ali Talukder and thus the plaintiffs are the co-shares of the suit land and which are ejmali land as such claimed saham.

43. We have examined all the documents but no where it is found that Mohammad Ali Talukder was the original owner of the suit land. Though the plaintiffs claimed that Mohammad Ali Talukder is the owner of the suit land and the plaintiffs claimed that Tofani Talukder is also the owner of the rest portion of the land. It appears that the CS record was not prepared in the name of Tofani Talukder and Mohammad Ali Talukder but which were prepared in the name of Syed Ali Talukder and Amjad Ali Talukder the two sons of Tofani Talukder and the name of Abdul Hakim Talukder the son of Mohammad Ali Talukder. It appears that the defendant No. 64 and 65 sisters of Abdul Hakim Talukder. The CS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Hakim alone but three sisters of Abdul Hakim did not challenge the CS record. Since it is the case of the plaintiffs that the CS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Hakim Talukder Hakimuddin and two sons of Tofani Talukder Sayed Ali Talukder and Amjad Ali Talukder in such a case they ought to have challenged the CS record.

44. It is settled principle that the plaintiffs should prove their case by adducing evidence. In the instant case the plaintiffs failed to prove that the suit land was settled in favour of Mohammad Ali Talukder and Tofani Talukder. But on perusal of the CS record it is found that the CS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Hakim Talukder and two sons of Tofani Talukder namely Sayed Ali Talukder and Amjad Ali Talukder. The plaintiff's side failed to produce any witness in support of the case that the land was settled in favour of Mohammad Ali Talukder and Tofani Talukder. Even on perusal of the Exhibit No. 3 it is found that Abdul Hakim Talukder transferred some land on 27-3-1943 before SA record. So, it is clear that the defendant No. 1 was the only owner of the suit land. But the trial court did not consider the said documentary evidence and erroneously decided that the original owner was Mohammad Ali Talukder. It appears that the successive heirs of Rukubjan claimed their saham by purchase and inheritance. They claimed that entire portion of the land of defendant No. 64 and 65 the two sisters of Abdul Hakim purchased by plaintiff Nos. 11 and 12.

45. At the time of hearing of this appeal the plaintiffs amended the plaint claiming title of the suit land and also challenged the CS record.

46. Mr M Liton Ahmed the learned Advocate argued that as per provision of Article 91 of the Limitation Act, any instrument should be challenged within 3 years even as per Article 120 of the Limitation Act, and the Limitation is only 6 years. The CS record was prepared in the year 1919 and the suit was filed in the year 1967 but the plaintiffs now filed application for amendment of the plaint claiming title and challenging the CS record long after about 100 years. It appears that at the time of filing the suit three sisters of Abdul Hakim Rokabjan, Phuljan and Rupjan did not challenge the CS record claiming that the suit land was originally belonged to their father even they did not file any document that the said land was settled in favour of Mohammad Ali. In such circumstance of the facts, it is our view that the case challenging the CS record is clearly barred by limitation.

<u>47. The learned Advocate of the appellants submits that preparation of CS record under section 103(b) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 has presumptive value that every entry in a record-of-rights finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect. In support of his argument he cited the decision of the case of Hriday Ranjan Dey vs Niranjan Dey being dead his heirs, Probate Dey reported in 10 BLT (AD) 137 = 54 DLR (AD) 16 and the case of Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81 wherein the principle laid down that: "According to section 103(b)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act every entry in a record-of-rights finally published shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect."</u>

48. It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit land belonged to Tofani Talukder and Mohammad Ali Talukder. Though one of the successive heirs of Tofani Talukder deposed as DW-4 but in his deposition he did not claim that suit land was originally belonged to Tofani Talukder but he claimed that which was belonged to his father Amjad Ali Talukder and CS record was prepared in the name of Syed Ali Talukder and Amjad Ali Talukder. Plaintiffs also claimed that Abdul Hakim Talukder was minor when the CS record was prepared but no evidence from the side of the plaintiffs that he was minor at that time. The plaintiffs claimed that Tofani Talukder took initiative to prepare the CS record. But it is found that the CS record was not prepared in the name of Tofani Talukder which was prepared in the name of Syed Ali Talukder and Amjad Ali Talukder. So, it cannot be presumed that Tofani Talukder excluding the three daughters of Mohammad Ali Talukder namely Rokabjan, Phuljan and Rupjan recorded the land in the name of Abdul Hakim Talukder alone. But the trial court did not at all consider the said material facts of the case.

49. Mr Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent submits that the ownership of land on the basis of CS record is not a conclusive prove and in support of his argument he cited the decision of the case of Pramatha Nath Chowdhury vs Kamir Mondal reported in 17 DLR (SC) 392 wherein our Apex Court held: "The presumption that attaches to a record-of-right under section 103-B of the Bengal Tenancy Act, is only this that the entry in the record-of-right represents that correct state of the affairs of the date it was prepared. Whether that states of affairs is continued even afterwards is not a presumption which arises under this section but under section 114 of the evidence Act, and its probative diminishes value progressively with the laps of time. The older the record the loss in its presumptive valuable. This is a matter, therefore, of proof and it merely has the effect of shifting the onus upon the other side. It is certainly not a conclusive prove."

50. Admittedly, the CS record was pre-pared in the name of Abdul Hakim Talukder who was the original defendant No. 1. Even the plaintiffs did not produce any subsequent record that by which the CS record was corrected or revised. So the aforesaid decision does not support the case of the plaintiff.

<u>51. It is found that two sisters of Abdul Hakim Talukder Phuljan and Rupjan transferred some portion of the land in favour of Aftabuddin and Usafuddin. It appears that the defendant Nos. 11 and 12 claimed that Rokabjan and Phuljan by registered a kabla Exhibits-1 and 1(a) transferred the property in favour of defendant Nos. 11 and 12 in the year 1939 and 1942 and Amiruddin predecessor of the plaintiff No. 1-10 purchased 16 decimals land from defendant No. 6 by Kabla Exhibits-1(b) and 1(c) and also purr chased 10.14 decimals of land from defendant No. 2 by kabla Exhibits-1(d) and 1(e) and Nasiruddin husband of Rukubjan purchased 0.83 decimals by Exhibit-1(f) from the defendant No. 2 one of the son of Syed Ali the son of Tofani Talukder who was the CS recorded owner. (Since Syed Ali is the another CS recorded owner as such by the said purchase deed it cannot be said that the CS record was not rightly prepared in the name of defendant No. 1.) It appears that since the defendant No. 11 and 12 purchased land by Exhibits-1 and 1(a) in the year of 1939 and 1942 from Rokabjan and Phuljan though they have no right and title to transfer the property but the defendant No. 1 did not challenge the said deeds so, it is our view that by adverse possession they are entitled to get the said portion of the land.</u>

52. The trial court also considering the evidence on record about the saham of the other defendants took view that they are entitled to get their respective saham. On perusal of the findings of the trial court we find that the said findings are on the basis of the evidence. So, we do not interfere with the said findings of the trial court.

53. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, it is our view that at the time of appeal challenging the CS record is clearly barred by limitation. However, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the aforesaid observation it is our view that the judgment of the trial court should be modified. Thus we find merit in the appeal.

54. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part. The judgment and decree is hereby modified. The plaintiff Nos. 11-12 do get the saham of the land which was purchased from Rupjan and Rokabjan through registered deeds Exhibits 1-1(a) in the year of 1939 and 1942. The defendant Nos. 2-5 do get their saham excluding the portion which was transferred in favour of the plaintiffs and defendants plus 0.11 1/4 cents. The defendant No. 6-18 do get saham for 1.09 1/4 acres plus 0.07 3/4 cents of land. The defendant Nos. 55-66 do get saham for 0.91 acres in pursuance of the Heba deed Exhibit-A-III.

Send down the Lower Court's Records at once.

End.
